text:
sara: paging oncall — Sigma (enterprise VPC, eu-west-2) is reporting massive tail latency. p95 ~450ms, p99 ~2.8s for their dedicated pool. SLO is 300ms. Opening a live thread. @incident-bot can you post the alert details?
incident-bot: ALERT: sigma-prod-eu2: latency.p99 > 2.0s (observed 2.8s) — affected hosts: ded-pool-eu2-03..07 — triggered at 2026-03-15T09:34:16Z — pager routed to oncall (sara).
mano: on it. grabbing metrics now. looks like a sudden increase in long-tail request queueing.
eliot: checking model variants — Sigma pinned to rwd-13b-q8 but we have rwd-6b and rwd-13b-quant-ff. Could downgrade as quick mitigation.
kyra: are we sure it's model compute and not networking? infra graphs show CPU/GPU utilization on ded-pool is high but not saturated. queuing spikes at the request ingress layer.
sara: customer reports spikes started after a large batch job from a tenant (tenant_47) that runs nightly translations. Could be tenant noisy neighbor. Sasha — can you confirm with Sigma?
sasha: pinged customer SRE, they confirm a large scheduled batch at 09:20 UTC. They're pausing it now on their side. I'll keep them updated.
mano: good candidate for tenant isolation. Recommend throttling tenant_47 to 20r/s and rebalancing remaining traffic across warm-pool.
eliot: to be safe, propose these immediate steps: 1) enable per-tenant rate limit for tenant_47 2) move 25% of Sigma traffic to warm pool in eu-west-1 3) downgrade Sigma route to rwd-6b to cut p99 latency. Any objections?
kyra: agree. I'll run the tenant throttle and initiate flow-shift. handing off to infra runbook.
sara: do it. include the exact commands in thread so ops follow.
kyra: running commands now —
```
# throttle tenant
redwoodctl routes update --customer sigma --tenant tenant_47 --rate 20r/s --region eu-west-2
# move traffic
redwoodctl traffic shift --from ded-pool-eu2 --to warm-pool-eu1 --percent 25 --strategy gradual
# downgrade model (canary first)
redwoodctl rollout create --route sigma-prod --from-model rwd-13b-q8 --to-model rwd-6b --canary 5%
```
kyra: commands issued. watch for rollback flags.
mano: seeing immediate drop in request queue depth on pool hosts. p95 trending down. p99 still high but improving.
eliot: can we temporarily enable KV prefix caching for Sigma's most common prefixes? That should reduce token work for repeat calls.
sara: yes, enable cache policy Sigma-prod prefix '/v1/generate' ttl 2h.
mano: cache enabled. also toggled aggressive batching window from 10ms -> 25ms for the pool; will accept slight extra latency to reduce p99 tail.
sasha: customer acknowledged pause on batch, appreciates quick action. asking for ETA for SLA recovery to report back to their ops manager.
sara: tell them ~15–30m for p99 to return under 300ms if no other noisy tenant. we'll update in 10m.
deploy-bot: Rollout sigma-prod canary to rwd-6b: 5% started at 2026-03-15T09:48:12Z — no errors reported.
mano: monitoring shows canary requests succeeding with median latency ~120ms. p99 for canary 280ms.
eliot: warm-pool traffic shift reached 25% at 09:51 UTC. pool load balanced ok.
kyra: tenant throttle applied confirmed — tenant_47 currently at 18r/s. their queue drain looks healthy.
sara: good. starting on-call handoff notes for next rotation in 30m. we might need an extended incident page if p99 doesn't recover fully.
mano: posting short remediation checklist to ops-runbook: 1) keep tenant throttle 2) continue traffic split 3) monitor canary then ramp rollback/downgrade decisions 4) contact account team for contract SLO messaging.
sasha: message to customer sent: "We're seeing p99 spikes caused by an internal tenant batch job; we've throttled and shifted traffic; mitigation in progress. We'll update in 10m or sooner."
sara: quick ask — can someone capture a flamegraph of the inference process for ded-pool-eu2-05? need to confirm whether we have serialization or GC spikes.
eliot: grabbing flamegraphs now, will paste snippet if I see something obvious.
eliot: pasted short snippet — looks like KV cache miss handling and gRPC request deserialization are hot. will open follow-up with runtime team for micro-optimizations but not a blocker for current mitigations.
mano: p99 is now 410ms and trending down. still above 300ms but much better than 2.8s.
kyra: can we reduce batching window back to 15ms and keep warm-pool shift until end of customer's batch window?
sara: yes, cautiously reduce batching to 15ms in 10m if metrics stable. keep warm-pool shift for 1h.
sasha: customer asked about root cause and wants a blameless postmortem. I've scheduled a sync for 16:00 UTC and requested logs.
sara: thanks. I'm going to document timeline and handoff to night oncall in 25m. if p99 < 320ms for next 20m, we'll move to monitoring state.
mano: recorded mitigation steps in incident tracker: INC-2026-0457. tagging relevant owners.
incident-bot: RESOLVE candidate: p99 < 320ms sustained for 20m. Awaiting final confirmation.
sara: marking thread as active mitigation. will update thread at 10:20 UTC with final status. thanks team. :white_check_mark:
